basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/WhoisFreaks/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The WhoisFreaks solution for Microsoft Sentinel ingests WhoisFreaks threat intelligence and newly registered domain feeds through an Azure Function and the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API. The solution includes a unified KQL parser, analytics rules for TI and NRD matches, hunting queries, and an overview workbook. **Data Connectors:** 1, **Parsers:** 1, **Workbooks:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 2, **Hunting Queries:** 3 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This Solution installs the data connector for WhoisFreaks. You can get WhoisFreaks custom log data in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

The Solution installs a parser that transforms the ingested data into Microsoft Sentinel normalized format. The normalized format enables better correlation of different types of data from different data sources to drive end-to-end outcomes seamlessly in security monitoring, hunting, incident investigation and response scenarios in Microsoft Sentinel.

link.label: Learn more about connecting data sources

options.text: This Microsoft Sentinel Solution installs workbooks. Workbooks provide a flexible canvas for data monitoring, analysis, and the creation of rich visual reports within the Azure portal.
WhoisFreaks overview: ingestion volume, feed breakdown, top TLDs, NRD age, and threat-domain activity.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, manage analytic rules in the Analytics blade.

elements.name: analytic1
elements.label: WhoisFreaks - Threat domain observed in environment

options.text:
Matches WhoisFreaks malware, phishing, or spam domains against DNS, proxy, firewall, and email telemetry.
A hit indicates a host or user in the environment contacted a domain listed by WhoisFreaks as malicious.

elements.name: analytic2
elements.label: WhoisFreaks - Contact with newly registered domain

options.text:
Detects internal hosts contacting a domain that appears in WhoisFreaks newly registered domain (NRD) feeds
and was registered within the last N days (default 7). Newly registered domains are frequently used in
phishing and malware campaigns shortly after registration.
This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run them from the Hunting blade.

elements.name: huntingquery1
elements.label: WhoisFreaks - Threat domains in DNS activity

options.text:
Joins WhoisFreaks malware/phishing/spam domains with DnsEvents over the last 7 days.
Use to hunt for historical contact with known-bad domains after enabling the connector. This hunting query depends on WhoisFreaks data connector (WhoisFreaksMalware_CL WhoisFreaksPhishing_CL WhoisFreaksSpam_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery2
elements.label: WhoisFreaks - NRD contact via proxy or firewall

options.text:
Finds CommonSecurityLog / proxy traffic to domains present in WhoisFreaks NRD feeds
registered in the last 14 days. Useful for investigating fresh domain infrastructure. This hunting query depends on WhoisFreaks data connector (WhoisFreaksNRDGtldWithWhois_CL WhoisFreaksNRDCctldWithWhois_CL WhoisFreaksNRDGtldWithoutWhois_CL WhoisFreaksNRDCctldWithoutWhois_CL Parser or Table)

Lists WhoisFreaks threat-intelligence domains with confidence >= 0.8 (or missing confidence)
observed in the last 7 days. Use as a seed list for blocklists or deeper investigation. This hunting query depends on WhoisFreaks data connector (WhoisFreaksMalware_CL WhoisFreaksPhishing_CL WhoisFreaksSpam_CL Parser or Table)
